clues: This city stands by the Belaya River, west of the south Ural hills. It is the chief city of Bashkortostan in Russia.
Winters here are harsh, yet summers can run long and hot. Its coldest day ever fell on New Year's Day in 1979, a mark of deep frost.
This city was founded in 1574, when a fort was built here by order of Ivan the Terrible. That fort was the seed from which the whole city grew.
In one year, 2015, this city hosted two great world summits. Heads of the BRICS lands and one more big bloc all met here in that same year.
A big oil firm, Bashneft, keeps its head home in this city. Oil refining is a chief trade here, with chem and machine works close by.
